name: Pixtral-12B-2409
notes: TWO-PART MODEL, and the cost profile here is the outlier in this slice. (1) Vision: ViT, 24 layers, hidden 1024, 16 heads, patch_size 16, image_size 1024, intermediate 4096, rope_theta 1e4. There is NO spatial merge: every 16x16 patch becomes one LLM token. (2) LLM: Mistral dense decoder, dim 5120, n_layers 40, n_heads 32 / n_kv_heads 8, head_dim 128, hidden_dim 14336, vocab 131,072, rope_theta 1e9, max_position 131,072. ARCHITECTURE = dense. ACTIVATION is null: params.json does not state it (not published in any machine-readable form). VISION TOKENS -- THE HEADLINE NUMBER: a 1024x1024 tile is (1024/16)^2 = 4,096 ViT patches = 4,096 LLM tokens, one token per patch with no pooling whatsoever. Pixtral splits large images into 1024x1024 tiles; a 4096x4096 image is a 4x4 grid = 16 tiles = 65,536 VISION TOKENS. (Mistral's processor caps the tile count via max_num_tiles, so a serving config will lower this -- but the per-tile cost of 4,096 tokens is fixed by the architecture.) DOMINANCE: VISION DOMINATES CATEGORICALLY. Even one 1024x1024 tile (4,096 tokens) is 4x a typical 1,000-token text prompt, and multi-tile inputs reach tens of thousands of tokens. Compare: the same image at 1024x1024 through InternVL3 (448 tiles + 2x2 pixel shuffle) costs ~2,048 tokens, so Pixtral pays ~2x the prefill of InternVL3 and ~16x Qwen2.5-VL (256 tokens at 448x448) for the same pixels. Pixtral is the worst vision-token-per-pixel model in this slice. KV CACHE: 40 * 8 * 128 * 2 * 2 = 163,840 B/token (160 KiB) -- the largest per-token KV of any VLM recorded here. At 131,072 ctx that is 20.0 GiB per sequence at bf16. params_b 12.0 is MISTRAL'S OWN FIGURE, NOT verified from tensors: the repo ships consolidated.safetensors with no HF config.json (404) and the API reports no safetensors parameter metadata. Flagged as a vendor claim; treat as +/-. params.json is Mistral's reference config and is the source for every dimension field.
